table.brief: Hebrew timetable with rowspan day groups and long notes

understanding.purpose: A weekly class timetable (grade י'2, semester א') read by day: a reader finds the day, then scans across the lesson block for time, subject, teacher and room, and finally reads the note that qualifies the lesson (homework, group split, room change, cancellation).
understanding.reading: Right-to-left, top-to-bottom. The eye anchors on the merged day label, then runs leftwards through שעה → מקצוע → מורה → חדר, with הערות as an optional trailing annotation. Comparison is mostly vertical within a day (times march down in order) and across days for the same subject/teacher; the room number is the value a reader most often plucks out in isolation.
groups: יום + שעה — the 'when' pair; the day cell is a merged anchor for 2–3 consecutive rows, so it frames the time column
מקצוע + מורה + חדר — the lesson identity triplet read as one sweep and the core of the scan
הערות — a separate annotation layer, not a peer of the triplet; it is prose, not a short field
keep_intact: time ranges 08:15–09:00 etc. (78px unbreakable — must never break at the dash or wrap)
teacher names (אבי שפירא, רונית לוי, מיכל אדרי)
may_wrap: הערות — long free prose (up to 619px on one line); it may wrap to 2–4 lines and the merged day cell already gives those rows vertical room
header words שעה/מקצוע/מורה/חדר if needed, but only at word boundaries
understanding.note: Only the widths are under control; total must stay ≤628px. Because the day column is row-merged, extra height from wrapped notes does not break the row-unit reading — but very long notes will visibly stretch the whole row.

preferred.name: r0B
preferred.note: Give the scan-critical fields real slack — שעה gets 11px of breathing room so time ranges can never break at the dash, חדר and מורה get a few pixels — while הערות still takes roughly a third of the table.

acceptable.name: r0A
acceptable.note: Spine at true minimums (each of יום/שעה/מקצוע/מורה/חדר gets exactly its one-line width) and every spare pixel to הערות, so notes read in 3 lines and the short fields never wrap — the most compact vertical table.

bad.name: r0C
bad.note: Treat the lesson triplet מקצוע/מורה/חדר as three near-equal, calm columns and let הערות shrink to 175px (notes wrap to 3–4 lines); rows grow taller but the grid reads as an even rhythm rather than one dominant prose column.
bad.why: The notes column is squeezed to 175px while time, subject, teacher, and room get more width than they need for one-line content. That forces five-line notes cells, a 669px table, and uneven row heights (94/73/114), making the table unnecessarily tall and visually unbalanced.

rationale: r0B is the best balance: every header and identifier stays on one line, the notes column holds most entries in three lines, and the body rows keep an even 73px rhythm. r0A is also publishable and more compact, but its schedule columns sit exactly at their one-line minimums, leaving little breathing room and producing one shorter 53px row. r0C misallocates width by widening already-comfortable columns while over-wrapping the only prose column, so the table becomes tall and uneven without gaining readability.

general: Give width first to the column that must wrap long prose; once identifier and time columns fit on one line, extra width there buys little and can starve the prose column.
A small width buffer around the longest unbreakable word prevents exact-fit columns from looking cramped or becoming fragile.
Consistent body-row heights and clear column roles help readers scan a timetable as repeated units rather than as unrelated rows.
specific: Here the notes column is the only multi-line column, so its width largely controls table height and row rhythm.
The time, subject, teacher, and room columns all fit on one line within roughly 77–110px; widening them beyond that adds white space, not information.
The merged day cells mean row heights are driven mainly by notes length, making the notes-column width the critical proportion in this table.

tradeoffs: A reasonable designer could prefer r0A for its compactness and wider notes, accepting exact-fit columns and the shorter 53px row. r0B trades about 20px of height for more uniform row rhythm and small width buffers; the main disagreement is how much width the notes column deserves relative to the one-line schedule columns.
uncertain: Whether r0A's 53px row reads as efficient compression or as a broken rhythm, whether notes below about 195px still avoid excessive wrapping, and whether r0B's uniform rows justify the extra vertical white space.

critique.good: Best balance: every short field column is at its one-line minimum (57/99/77/81/88), so the remaining 226px goes to the only prose column. Headers stay unwrapped, there are no mid-word splits, and times, rooms and names remain intact. The wide left-hand note column reads as an annotation layer, while the merged day anchor stays clear.
critique.problems: No material layout fault. Notes still run 3–4 lines and drive the 548px height, but that is the unavoidable cost of the 628px budget; giving notes less width only makes the table taller.
critique.cause: Widths are exactly the minima: day 36+21, time 78+21, subject 56+21, teacher 60+21, room 67+21; the residual 226px is all that can be given to הערות.

critique.good: Short columns get a little extra breathing room and rows are more uniform at 73px; nothing wraps in headers or short fields.
critique.problems: Taller overall (568px) and noisier note wrapping: notes at 200px need more lines, including a 4-line last row. The extra 28px spent on day/time/subject/teacher/room buys no readability because those fields already fit on one line.
critique.cause: Widths exceed the minima by 5+11+3+4+5=28px, taken directly from הערות (226→200).

critique.good: The short columns are the most comfortable of the three, and the timetable fields are easy to isolate.
critique.problems: Visually too tall and unbalanced: notes at 175px wrap to 4–5 lines, rows grow to 94/114px, and the table reaches 669px. The note column becomes a narrow text tower, slowing the day scan.
critique.cause: 51px is moved from הערות (226→175) into day/time/subject/teacher/room, where it adds no value beyond one-line fit.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

ref_equal.why: The notes column is starved (~105px) while the day column is hugely over-wide; notes wrap into 6–8 lines and rows become very tall, with wasted white space in hour/teacher/subject.

r0B.why: Well proportioned: notes receives the surplus (~165px), the day column is compact, and hour, teacher, subject and room stay on one line; rows scan cleanly.

r0C.why: Near-ideal balance: room column sits at its one-line width, notes gets ~155px, day ~85px; all critical identifiers stay intact and only notes wrap naturally.

ref_auto.why: Notes is over-allocated (~200px) while hour, teacher and room fall below one-line widths; times split at the dash, names wrap, and rooms such as 'מעבדה 1' break across lines, disrupting scanning.

r0A.why: Close to C: compact day column, adequate room, notes ~155px; critical fields stay readable, though notes gets slightly less width and the room column looks tighter than in C.

raw.unsure: Exact pixel widths are estimated from the renders; B vs C is very close, and I am not fully certain whether E's room column causes 'אולם ספורט' to wrap.

r0B.why: Reasonable balance and no broken words, but the notes column (the only genuinely long content) is squeezed to roughly 200px, so every row grows to 5–7 lines while time/subject/teacher/room sit half-empty. Rows no longer read as compact units.

ref_equal.why: Notes are crushed to about 130px, forcing one long paragraph per row into 8–10 narrow lines, while room, teacher and subject columns carry large empty areas. The table becomes a tall stack of ragged text strips instead of a scannable schedule.

r0C.why: Slightly more width to notes than A and a tighter time column, so rows are shorter and the day/time/subject/teacher/room block stays readable. Still more whitespace in the middle columns than necessary and notes wrap more than they need to.

r0A.why: Notes get the dominant share (roughly 330px), collapsing the longest cell to 3–4 lines, while day, time, subject, teacher and room are sized to their content and stay intact. Rows are compact, the time ranges read on one line, and the vertical rhythm is even across all six rows.

ref_auto.why: The time column is too narrow: '08:15–09:00' and similar ranges break across two lines, destroying the primary scan axis of a timetable, and teacher names ('אבי שפירא', 'מיכל אדרי') and room text also split. Notes get only moderate width, so the table is tall and hard to compare.

raw.unsure: Widths were estimated by eye from the renders; small differences between A and C could shift their relative ranking, and I cannot verify exact pixel sums against the 628px budget.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
